system.name: GRACE
system.one_liner: a loss-resilient real-time video system built on a neural video codec jointly trained under packet losses

content.subject: how GRACE's reversible random packetization maps tensor elements to packets so a lost packet only zeroes its mapped elements

content.key_idea: A reversible pseudo-random mapping lets GRACE convert real packet loss into the same effect as the random element-zeroing used during training, so the encoder and decoder are jointly loss-aware.
content.reading_order: left to right then down and up: frame into the NN Encoder and coded tensor, through partitioning to the lost packet, then up through merging and the NN Decoder to the decoded frame.

evidence: GRACE employs reversible randomized packetization as shown in Figure 5.
an x% packet loss rate has the effect of randomly zeroing x% of the values in the encoder's output tensor
GRACE's reversible randomized packetization. The tensor elements mapped to a lost packet will be set to zeros.

summary: Figure 5 explains GRACE's reversible randomized packetization, the mechanism that lets the system simulate packet loss consistently between training and deployment. On the left, the sender's NN Encoder produces a coded tensor from the original frame; a numbered 3x3 grid stands in for this tensor's elements. Random partitioning applies a reversible pseudo-random mapping that scatters the numbered elements across three colour-coded sub-tensors, each entropy-coded into one packet for transmission. On the right, one packet is lost in transit (crossed out); because the mapping is reversible, the decoder knows exactly which tensor positions that packet held and zeroes only those elements (shown as blank cells) while merging the surviving sub-tensors back into a coded tensor for the NN Decoder to reconstruct the decoded frame. The worked 1-9 numbering lets the reader trace precisely which values survive and which become zero.
summary_zh: 图5展示GRACE的可逆随机分包机制：编码张量按随机映射拆分为三个彩色子张量并打包发送；一个包丢失后，解码端依据同一映射仅将对应位置清零，再合并重建张量用于解码。
